correctness.rationale: Reconstructed unique ell_p duality map and scalar positive sequence variational G_F=t u1 u2^(p-1)+sum_(n>=2) u_n u_(n+1)^(p-1), G_B=t u1^(p-1)u2+sum tail. Young inequalities bound the tails by all mass except the exceptional edge, leaving exact two-variable inequalities a^p+(p-1)b^p/p >=p^(1/p)a b^(p-1) and a^p+b^p/p>=q^(1/q)a^(p-1)b. Optimizing gives ratios a/b=p^(-1/p) and (a/b)^p=(p-1)/p, so both thresholds are sharp. At or below threshold equality of every tail Young edge would force nonzero constant infinite ell_p tail, impossible; distant flat blocks show radii still equal one but never attained. For supercritical t, the explicit geometric tail u1=a, u_n=s^(n-2) has limiting positive excess as s increases to 1. Reflexivity, coordinatewise convergence and a tail energy <=tail mass give rho<=G(u)+1-||u||^p; rho>1 forces ||u||=1 and attainment. Independently evaluated exact optimizer equalities for p=1.5,2,3,4,10. p=3,t=4/3 falls between thresholds with forward=1 and backward>1. Valid for both scalar fields, including t=0 and equality threshold.
residual_risks: No exact formula claimed for numerical radii above one, just exceedance and attainment.
Excluded p=1 and p=infinity where reflexivity breaks and norming functional uniqueness changes.

value.rationale: An exact structural transition in the natural one-defect perturbation of the canonical unilateral shift, with nonlinear conjugate-exponent directional asymmetry and simultaneous attainment criterion, extends a recognized Hilbert phenomenon to all non-Hilbert ell_p. The exact thresholds are meaningful boundary data; no arbitrary parameter slice or only numerical experiment.
residual_risks: The p=2 threshold is not novel; scientific contribution resides in p unequal 2 and both directions, not in any exact supercritical radius formula.

final_claim: For real or complex ell_p with 1<p<infinity and one first-edge weight t>=0, forward unilateral shift numerical radius equals 1 exactly for t<=p^(1/p), backward radius equals 1 exactly for t<=q^(1/q) (q=p/(p-1)); neither attains its radius in the unit regime and both attain it above.
limitations: Only one exceptional first edge and 1<p<infinity; supercritical radius size not calculated.
Possible earlier unindexed non-Hilbert shift comparison is residual literature risk.
